A Petition of the Merchants and Tradesmeh of the Pet;t;on from Town of Wakefield, in the West Riding of the County Wakefield of York, was presented to the House, and read; Setting " 3 forth, That the Petitioners are apprehensive that any Alteration in the now existing Laws concerning the Responsibility of Ship or Sloop Owners for Goods in-trusted to their Care would greatly endanger the Safety of Trade, and become the Source of innumerable Disputes; and that the Petitioners learn, with great Anxiety and Alarm, that the Owners, Mailers, and Mariners of Sloops and Vessels, passing on Rivers where the Tide flows, are endeavouring to exonerate and discharge themselves from the usual Responsibility in same of Lots or Damage (except in Cafes of actual Negligence) and as thele, in moll instances, would be extremely difficult to prove, the offending Party alone being competent to furnish the Evidence required, the Petitioners are of Opinion, that to exempt Inland Carriers by Water from the same Responsibility to

which

v

fyi r

which Garriers by Land are liable (since their Rates are arbitrary, and proportioned to their Rilks) would be to destroy that Confidence and Security so necefi-fary in the Conveyance of Goods both by Land and by Water; and that the Petitioners beg Leave further to state, that the Owners of Sloops trading in the Tideway of the River Humber have, within the last Twelve Months, advanced their Rates of Freight from Selby to Hull (being the Course of the Tideway) from Four Shillings and Six Pence per Ton to Seven Shillings and Six Pence per Ton, which they deemed fully adequate to their Rifles, and with which the Petitioners have complied: And therefore praying. That the Bill presented to the House in Favour of the Ship or Sloop Owners may not pass into a Law. fvtition from A Petition of the Merchants, Manufacturers, and Huddersfield Tradesmen of the Town and Parish of Huddersfield, in ©whers Bill. the County of York, was also presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the Bill for giving Relief to the Owners and Matters of Ships; and Setting forth, That, when the said Bill was first brought into the House, the Petitioners did not make any Objection thereto, but they now learn, with great Anxiety and Alarm, that an Amendment has been made to the Bill, containing Matter quite foreign to its original Object,

namely, to exonerate and discharge from the usual Responsibility, in same of Loss or Damage, the Owners, Masters, and Mariners, of Sloops and Vessels passing on Rivers where the Tide flows, except in Cafes of actual Negligence; and likewise containing the same Allegations as the preceding Petition: And therefore praying, That the Amendment proposed to the said Bill be rejected, and that the Bill, as originally proposed do pass into a Law.

Petition from A Petition of the thereunder-signed Merchants, and

others, feliding at Leeds, and its Neighbourhood, in the County of York, who are deeply concerned in the shipping and receiving Goods by Vessels trading from the Port of Hull, was likewise presented to the House, and read; Also taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth. That, if the same should pass into a Law, it will materially injure their Interest, and the Commercial Interests of this Kingdom inasmuch as it will first destroy that Part of the Common Law which charges Carriers by Water with Responsibility to the Shippers of Merchandize for any Loss or Damage happening to such Merchandize while in the Custody, or Under the Care, of such Carriers: Secondly, exonerate all Carriers by Water from Responsibility, not only for Any Damage to, or Loss of Merchandize in their Custody which may have happened previous to this Time, but also from any Loss or Damage which may hereafter happen, except in Cafes of Negligence or Misconduct by such Carriers: Thirdly, charge the Petitioners, and other Shippers of Goods, with Losses which, in many probable Cafes, might, with proper Attention, be foreseen and prevented by the Carriers and their Servants, or against which the Ship Owners can always insure, or indemnify themselves by railing their Freight in proportion to the Risk, while the Petitioners, and other Shippers of Goods, can neither fore- . lee nor prevent the Evil, nor will they have any Means of Redress, but by proving either Misconduct or Negligence in the Matter or Mariners of the Vessels, who being the Persons guilty of such Neglect, it mutt be apparent to the House, that they can never be expected to criminate themselves: Lastly, the Provisions of the Bill extend not only to Vessels trading in Rivers where the Tide flows, but they virtually extend to all Inland Navigation communicating with such Rivers, hecaulc, in same of Loss or Damage to Goods, it will oblige the Owner of them, before he can have any Re-dress from the Carrier, to prove that the Loss or Damage happened out of the Tideway, and it will be . nearly an Imjx>flibility to prove in any same where or

how the Loss or Damage may have happened: And *

JuUi. \ 1797,

therefore praying the House to reject such particular Clauses of the said Bill as relate to Vessels navigating any Rivers, Creeks, Harbours, or any other Place, so far as the Tide flows, and not suffer the same to pals into a Law, and that the Petitioners may be heard, by themselves, and their Counsel, against the said Bill passing into a Law.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to be referred to the Consideration of the Committee to whom the said Bill is committed; and the last mentioned Petitioners are to be heard, by themselves, or Counsel, before the said Committee, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That it be aninstruction to the said Committee, That they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said last mentioned Petition.

A Petition of the thercunder-signed Persons, Merchants redding at Nottingham, and employing Owners and Mailers of Ships and Vessels in the Carriage of Goods and Merchandize, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the Bill forgiving Relief to the Owners and Mailers of Ships; and Setting forth, That, it the said Bill should pals into a Law', it will overthrow a main Pillar of that System under which Commerce has been reared and supported, and, by lapping Security, will enervate Enterprize, to the manifell Injury of the Kingdom, both with regard to the Property of Individuals and the Revenue of the State; and that the Ship Owners and Mailers, with the Law in View (as it now ilands) are impelled by Interest to be careful in the Chuice of the Mariners, and to be vigilant over their Conduct, in which elfential Points of Duty it is evident they would relax, if released from Responsibility; the same Realoning fully applies to the State and Condition of the Shipping employed; and the Petitioners observe, that the Modification of the Bill in the Committee, which confines its Operation to the high Seas and Tideway of Rivers, is not an useful Modification to the Inhabitants of Nottingham or any other Inland Situation, because it is, in moll Inllances, impossible to ascertain on what Part of the Navigation the Loss or Damage was sustained; and that the Petitioners forbear commenting on the Injultice of introducing an ex pqd Facio Law, or the Clause giving Damages in Cafes of wilful Neglect, as it is palpable that Persons guilty of Neglect will not criminate themselves, and through no other Channel can Evidence flow': The Alarm of the Petitioners is created by the Principle of the Bill; which no Melioration can render safe: And therefore praying, That the Ship Owners and Mailers may not be released from that Responsibility which the Law now enjoins.

Lunas 10° die Julit Anno 37° Georgii III,n Regis, 1797 - Prayers.

A Petition of the Mailer, Wardens, Searchers, and Assistants, of the Company of Cutlers, within Hallamshire, in the County of fork, and of the Merchants, Manufacturers, and Tradesmen,oftheTown and Neighbourhood of Sheffield, in the said County of York, was presented to the House, and read j Taking Notice of the Bill for giving Relief to the Owners and Mailers of Ships; and Setting forth, That the same will, if passed into a Law, essentially injure the Commercial Interests of this Kingdom, for the following Reasons: First, that it releases all Owners and Mailers of Ships or Vessels from Responsibility for any Damage to, or Loss of, Merchandize in their Custody, which may hereafter happen, except in Cafes of Negligence or Misconduct by such Owners and Mailers; and, although the Onus probanda, in same of such Damage or Loss, is to fall entirely upon the said Owners and Mailers, the Petitioners conceive that this obviates in a very imperfect Manner the general Objections to the Principle of the Bill, which tends to endanger the Safety of Trade, and to become the Source of innumerable Disputes: — Secondly, That it also operates as an ex FaSio Law, by releasing Owners and Mailers of Ships and Vessels from Responsibility for Damage of Merchandize which has happened previous to the Time of passing the said Act, and therefore appears highly objeftionable in this Point of View: — Thirdly, That although the Provisions of the Bill extend only to Ships upon the High Seas, and to Vessels trading in Rivers where the 'Fide flows, yet virtually they extend to all Inland Navigations communicating with Rivers where the said Tide so flows, becaufeof the Difficulty of ascertaining at what particular Part of any River the said Loss or Damage may happen, and whether out of the Tideway or not: — Fourthly,'That the Petitioners against the Bill throughout the Kingdom have not had sufficient Time or Opportunity afforded them to oppose the same with every Argument which may be adduced against it, and therefore that, in a Matter of such great Commercial Import, the Bill should not, in the Opinion of the Petitioners, on any Account, be suffered to pass into a Law this Session: And therefore praying the House to reject the said Bill in toto.

A Petition of the thereunder-signed Persons, Merchants, and others, residing in the Borough of Penryn, and employing Owners and Matters of Ships and Vessels, in the Carriage of Goods and Merchandize, was also presented to the House, and read; likewise taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, That, if the same should pass into a. Law, it will materially injure their Interests, and the Commercial Interests of this Kingdom, inasmuch as it will, First, completely destroy that Part of the Common Law which charges Carriers by Water with Responsibility to the Shippers of Merchandize for Loss or Damage happening to such Merchandize, whilst in the Custody, and under the Care, of such Carriers: Secondly, release all Carriers by Water from Responsibility for Damage to, or Lois of Merchandize in their Custody, and under the:r Care, which has happened previous to this Time: Thirdly, release all Carriers by Water from Responsibility for any Damage to, or Loss of, Merchandize in their Custody, and under their Care, which may hereafter happen, except in Cafes of Negligence and Misconduct by such Carriers; and consequently, Fourthly, charge the Petitioners, and other Shippers of Goods, with Losses which, in most probable Cafes, may, by due Care, be foreseen and prevented by Carriers ana their Servants, but which the Petitioners, and other Shippers of Goods, cannot have the Power of prevent-

The postponed Order of the Day, for taking into further Consideration the Report which was made from the Committee, to whom the Bill for giving Relief to the Owners and Matters of Ships, was re-committed, being read;

A Petition of the thereunder-signed Merchants, Manufacturers, and other Traders, of the Town of Manchester, employing Owners and Matters of Ships and Vessels in the Conveyance of Goods, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, That, if the same should pass into a Law, the Consequences mutt seriously affect the Safety of their Trade, as well as the Commercial Interests of the Kingdom at large; and that the protective Security of the Common Law, under which Carriers by Water are responsible for the Loss or Damage of Goods entrusted to their Care, would be subverted, and such Carriers would be fully exonerated from the Losses and Damages already happened, and also (except in Cafes of their Neglect or Misconduct) those which may hereafter happen; and that the Difficulty of making out by Proof any Negligence or Misconduct of the Carriers, or their Servants, will for the most Part operate as a complete Bar to the Claim, the Matters and Mariners, with whom the Culpability will generally rest, being the only probable Witnesses capable of furnishing sufficient Evidence of the Fact; and that the proposed Abridgment of Responsibility will evidently render more frequent Lottes, which a careful Attention in the Carriers and their Servants might probably have avoided; and, wfiilft the Shippers are unable to prevent such Losses, or reduce them by Insurance, the Ship Owners, by proportioning the Freight to the Risk, may be amply insured; and that, if those, who claim for Losses against Carriers on Inland Navigations, are bound to prove that such Losses happened out of the Tideway, this Fact cannot in many Instances be shewn, for, as the Bill extends to Rivers where the Tide flows, it will also in Effect extend to Inland Navigations communicating with Rivers where the Tide flows, and the Bill, if fanCtioned by the Legislature, would otherwise become the Source of much Litigation: And therefore entreating the House, That they will not permit the above-mentioned Bill to pass into a Law.

A Petition of the thereunder-signed Merchants reading in the Cities and Suburbs of London and IV

minster, and the Borough of , and employing

Owners and Matters of Ships and Vessels in the Carriage of Goods and Merchandize, was also presented to the House, and read; likewise taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth. That, if the same should pass into a Law, it will materially injure their Interests, and the Commercial Interests of this Kingdom, inasmuch as it will, First, completely destroy that Part of the Common Law which charges Carriers by Water with Responsibility to the Shippers of Merchandize for Loss or Damage happening to such Merchandize whilst in the Custody, and under the Care, of such Carriers: Secondly, release all Carriers by

Water from Responsibility for Damage to, or Loss of Merchandize in their Custody, and under their Care, which has happened previous to this Time: Thirdly, release all Carriers by Water from the Responsibility for any Damage to, or Loss of, Merchandize in their Custody, and under their Care, which may hereafter happen, except in Cafes of Negligence or Misconduct by such Carriers; and consequently. Fourthly, charge the Petitioners and others. Shippers of Goods, with Lottes which, in most probable Cafes, may, by due Care, be foreseen and prevented by the Carriers and ,their Servants, but which the Petitioners and others.

Shippers of Goods, cannot have the Power of preventing, and may not be able to insure against, but which the Ship Owners may insure against by railing their Freight in Proportion to the Riik: Fifthly, if such Lottes happen by the Negligence or Miscondud: of the Carriers or their Servants, the Petitioners and other Shippers of Goods will have no Remedy but by proving such Negligence or Misconduct, the Difficulty of which will he apparent to the House, inasmuch as the Matter and Mariners of Vessels are the only Persons who are likely to prove and be guilty of the fame:

Lastly, the Provisions of the Bill extend not only to Ships upon the High Seas, and Vessels trading only in Rivers where the Tide flows, but virtually extend to all Inland Navigations communicating with Rivers where the Tide flows, because, in Cafes of Loss or Damage to Goods, it will oblige the Owner of them, before he can make the Carrier liable, to prove the Loss or Damage happened out of the Tideway, and, in many Cafes, it will be impossible to prove where or how the Loss or Damage happened: And therefore praying the House wholly to reject the said Bill, and not suffer the same to pass into a Law.

A Petition of the thereunder-signed Persons, Mer- Petitions from chants and Manufacturers redding at Bury, employing ®ury a"d Owners and Matters of Ships and Vessels in the against shTp Carriage of Goods and Merchand ize: And also, Owners Bill.

That extensive Injuries to the Petitioners Trade, and the general Commercial Interests of the Kingdom, mutt necessarily arise from the Operations of the said Bill, in case the same should pass into a Law; and that, independent of the immediate Mischiefs relulting from the Destruction of the Common Law, a6 applied to the Responsibility of Carriers, the Difficulty of adducing satisfactory Evidence in Cafes of actual Negligence or Misconduct, to which Responsibility is proposed to be confined, would generally defeat the just Claims for Compensations, in respect of the Loss or Damage occasioned by either of those Causes; and that, as a proportionate Advancement of Freight affords Means of Indemnification to the Carrier, whilst the Shippers may be unable to inlure against Losses, which, under the legislative Authority now fought for, they would be bound to l'ultain, and as those Losses are more likely to occur by diminishing the established Responsibility of the Carrier, the Petitioners on thele Grounds submit the Justice and Propriety of continuing such Responsibility unaltered; and that, by necessary Construction, the Bill appears to extend to Inland Navigations communicating with Rivers where the Tide flows, and, if fane-tioned by Law, would, in various Respects, occasion

it will materially injure their interelb, and the Commercial Interests of this Kingdom, inasmuch as it will,

First, completely destroy that Part of the Common Law which charges Carriers by Water with Rel'pon-fibility to the Shippers of Merchandize for Lois or Damage happening to such Merchandize vvliillt in the Custody, and under the Care, of such Carriers: Secondly, releale all Carriers by Water from Respontibility for Damage to, or Loss of, Merchandize in their Custody, and under their Care, which has happened previous to this Time: Thirdly, releale all Carriers by Water from Rclponfibijity for any Damage to, or Lois of, Merchandize in their Custody, and under their Care, which may hereafter happen, except in Cafes of Negligence or Milcondudt by such Carriers; and consequently, Fourthly charge the Petitioners and others *

Shippers of Goods, with Losses which, in moll probable Cafes, may, by due Care, be forefecn and prevented by the Carriers and their Servants, but which the Petitioners and others, Shippers of Goods, cannot have the Power of preventing, and may not be able to insure against, but which the Ship Owners may insure against by railing their Freight in proportion to the Risk: Fifthly, if such Lolfes happen by the Negligence or Miscondud of the Carriers or their Servants, the Petitioners and other Shippers of Goods will have no Remedy but by proving such Negligence or Miscondud, the Diiiiculty cf which will be apparent to the House, inasmuch as the Master and Mariners of Vessels are the only Persons who are likely to prove and be guilty of the same: Lastly; the Provisions of the Bill extend not only to Ships upon the High Seas, and Vessels trading only in Rivers where the Tide flows but virtually extend to all Inland Navigations communicating with Rivers where the Tide flows, because, in Cafes of Loss or Damage to Goods, it will oblige the Owner of them, before he can make the Carrier liable, to prove the Loss or Damage happened out of the Tideway, and, in many Cafes, it will be impossible to prove where or how the Loss or Damage happened:

And therefore praying the House wholly to reject the said Bill, and not suffer the same to pass into a Law.

My Lords and Gentlemen,

I cannot put an End to this Session of Parliament, without returning you My most sincere and coiyiial Thanks, for the Assiduity and Zeal with which you have applied yourselves to the important Objects which have required your Attention, and for the Wisdom and Firmncls which you have manifested in the new and difficult Emergencies for which you have had to provide.

I mull particularly express the just Sense I entertain of the salutary and effectual Provisions which you made for {Lengthening the Means of National Defence, and the Measures adopted for obviating the Inconveniencies which were to be apprehended to Credit from the temporary Suspension of Payments in Cash by the Bank; as well as of the Promptitude, Vigour, and Effect, with which you afforded Me your Assistance and Support in l'uppressing the daring and treasonable Mutiny which broke out in a Part of My Fleet, and in ebun-terafting lo dangerous and pernicious an Example.

Commercial Engagements between the Two Countries have been renewed, in tuch a Manner as will, 1 doubt not, materially conduce to their mutual Interests.

Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

I must return you My particular Thanks for the liberal and extensive Provision which you have made for the various Exigencies of the Public Service; and, while I lament the Necessity which encreased them to so large an Amount, it is a Consolation to Me to observe the Attention you employed in distributing the heavy Burdens which they occasioned, in such a Manner as to render their Pressure as little severe as possible to My People.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

The Issue of the Important Negotiation in which I am engaged, is yet uncertain: But,'whatever may be the Event, nothing will have been Wanting, on My Part, to bring it to a successful Termination on such Conditions as may be confident with the Security, Honour, and elfential Intereds of My Dominions. In the mean Time, nothing can so much tend to forward the Attainment of Peace, as the Continuance of that Zeal, Exertion, and Public Spirit, of which My Subjects have given such conspicuousi and honourable Proofs, and of which the Perseverance and Firmness of Parliament has afforded them so driking an Example.

And afterwards, the Lord Chancellor, by His Majesty's Command, said,

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

It is His Majesty's Royal Will and Pleasure, that

this Parliament be prorogued to Thursday the 5th Day of October next, to be then here holden; and this Parliament is accordingly prorogued to Thursday the 5th Day of October next.

Jovisy 50 die OBobris;

Anno 37° Georgii III. 11 Regis, 1797.

THE House being met, pursuant to the lad Prorogation; and Mr. Speaker being in the Country,

A Message was brought from the Lords, by Mr. Quarme, Yeoman Ulher of the Black Rod:

Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

The'Lords, authorized by virtue of His Majesty s Commission, desire the immediate Attendance of this Honourable House, in the House of Peers, to hear the Commission read.

Accordingly the House, with the Clerk Alfidant, went up to the House of Peers: Where the Commission was read, for the further proroguing of the Parliament, until Thursday, the 2d Day of November next; and the Parliament was accordingly prorogued until Thursday, the ad Day of November next,
